newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - ABARE raises Australia aluminium export view.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - ABARE raises Australia aluminium export view.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday that it had not changed its forecast of Australian aluminium production in the year to June 30, 1997, but that it had raised its aluminium export forecast for 1996/97.
ABARE said in its September quarter commodities bulletin that it had left its forecast of production in 1996/97 unchanged at 1.38 million tonnes from its June quarter forecast.
However it said it had raised its aluminium export forecast for 1996/97 to 1.05 million tonnes from the 1.025 million tonne forecast in June.

ABARE said its 1.38 million tonnes production forecast for 1996/97 compared with actual production of 1.33 million tonnes in 1995/96. "Increases in output are expected to come from greater capacity use at the Boyne Island, Tomago, Kurri Kurri and Point Henry smelters," ABARE said.
It said its 1.05 million tonne export forecast for 1996/97 compared with actual exports in 1995/96 of 1.04 million tonnes.
"Aluminium export earnings are forecast to rise by around two percent to A$2.42 billion dollars in 1996/97," ABARE said.
"Increases in export volumes and higher world prices are expected to more than offset the effects on earnings of an assumed higher value of the Australian dollar," ABARE said.
ABARE forecast the world price of aluminium would rise to US$1,775 per tonne in 1996/97 from US$1,542 per tonne in 1995/96.
ABARE said Australian alumina production was forecast to rise only marginally to around 13.3 million tonnes in 1996/97 from the 13.29 million tonnes produced in 1995/96.
It forecast alumina exports would however fall to 10.63 million tonnes from 10.98 million tonnes in 1995/96.
"Alumina export earnings are forecast to rise by around eight percent to A$2.94 billion in 1996/97," ABARE said.
"Higher export unit values -- forecast to rise by around 16 percent -- will offset the effects of a forecast three percent decline in export volumes," the forecaster said.
